text:
jessica: Heads-up — customer (acct: acme-inc) opened ticket #3241 after they rotated IdP keys. SSO started failing for ~30% of users. Root error in our logs: 'RecipientNotFound' and 'AudienceRestrictionFailed'. They say they didn't change ACS on their side.
jessica: Paste of our auth log excerpt: `saml_response.validate(): Recipient='https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs' expected='https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs' -> false` — weirdly it shows expected equal but still failing.
sanjay: Can you attach the raw SAML response (redact PII) and their IdP metadata? Also did they change the EntityID or include whitespace?
jessica: Uploading snippets below. Customer metadata URL: https://idp.acme.local/metadata.xml (we fetched a copy). Their SP-assertionRecipient in signed assertion: `Recipient="https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs%20"` — note the trailing encoded space (%20). Their ACS configured in Console is `https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs` (no space).
sanjay: Ah. That sounds like an encoding mismatch during IdP rotation job that appended a space to the ACS in the new metadata. If assertion Recipient has trailing space it will not match strict compare.
kevin: Confirming we've seen two KeyDescriptor elements in their metadata: one with old cert (expired 2026-02-01) and one with new cert (rotated yesterday). The new metadata entry also contains an ACS with percent-encoded space. Snippet: ```xml
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.acme.local/idp">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <SingleSignOnService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect" Location="https://idp.acme.local/sso"/>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">...CERT...</KeyDescriptor>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
  <AssertionConsumerService index="0" Location="https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs%20" isDefault="true"/>
</EntityDescriptor>
```
alejandro: That ACS looks malformed — browsers might normalize %20 differently, and some IdP deploy scripts accidentally URL-encode spaces instead of trimming them. Our strict recipient check uses exact string equality (including percent-encoding).
sanjay: Repro steps for eng: 1) fetch customer metadata (we saved a copy) 2) send a SAML response with Recipient set to `https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs%20` and signed with their new cert 3) observe our verifier rejects with RecipientNotFound.
kevin: Quick mitigation: we can implement a tolerant compare that normalizes trailing spaces and decodes %20 for recipient matching for this customer only (short-term). Longer term we should add a forgiving mode behind a config flag per tenant.
jessica: Customer is P1 (payment processing block). They want a hotfix ASAP, but security wants to avoid loosening checks globally.
sam-oncall-bot: @sanjay requested an on-call rotation handoff to eng-saml with severity=P1 and link to ticket #3241.
sanjay: I'll take the lead. Plan: (A) deploy a targeted patch that trims and URL-decodes Recipient and Audience fields before equality check for this customer; (B) notify customer to re-publish metadata without encoded space and rotate again; (C) add an alert that flags encoded whitespace in incoming metadata during metadata refresh.
alejandro: Also add a validation step when we ingest metadata to warn if AssertionConsumerService Locations contain percent-encoding or trailing whitespace. We can fail ingest with a helpful error to avoid surprises.
jessica: I've told customer we can patch within 2 hours and will follow up with a safe rollback plan. I'll attach the saved metadata and the SAML response we used to repro to the ticket.
kevin: Logging note: add extra audit entry when we accept a normalized match for tenant X so we can track any potential replay/compatibility issues.
sanjay: Escalation to eng-saml done. I'll open an internal PR for the tolerant-compare with feature-flag and request a quick code review. Pinging @security for approval. :thinking_face:
jessica: Thanks — I'll update the customer and keep this thread posted.
